findings.issue: The findDetailsByIds javadoc says the batch 'makes no inventory call'. That is false. detail(p,false) still calls offerService.enrich, and OfferService.stockRows calls InventoryServiceClient.stockRows once per product. TD-BE-18 in this same PR says so. The unit test 'findDetailsByIdsKeepsOrderAndSkipsStock ... and no inventory call (B1)' only passes verifyNoInteractions(inventory) because OfferService is a @Mock, so its DisplayName overstates what it proves.
findings.fix: Change the javadoc to 'skips the per-variant stock call; offer enrichment still reads stock rows per product (TD-BE-18)'. Rename the test or its DisplayName to 'no variant-stock call'.

findings.issue: CTO condition 4 asks for a parity test showing detail=true is exactly the /{id} shape. The parity test uses seed products HEADSET, MOUSE and KEYBOARD, which have no variant stock to report. availableQuantity is then null both ways, so the one known difference (variant stock skipped) is never exercised. Parity is proven only where it holds trivially. This is documented in endpoints.md and does not affect checkout: order-service's Variant record has no availableQuantity (ignoreUnknown), OrderService reads no stock field, and OfferService's buy-box filter uses offer stock, which is still filled. So there is no change on the money path, but the deviation from 'exactly' should be stated rather than implied.
findings.fix: In the parity test, add a product that has variants (and an offer), and assert equality after stripping variants[].availableQuantity. Also assert that /{id} with a stubbed inventory carries a quantity that the batch omits, so the deviation is pinned explicitly.

findings.issue: AC-10 verifies times(1) only for batch(.., eq(true)). A stray batch(.., false) call or a second client would not be caught by this assertion. AC-10 also asks that the order be identical (variants, offers) to a per-line lookup, but the test checks only unitPrice, name, subtotal and currency. It does not check the line's variantId, offerId or sellerId. The pre-change failure was incidental (the unreachable real ProductViewFeignClient), but the post-change assertions do discriminate. A per-line or chunked batch fails times(1), and a single-id dedupe is asserted directly in AC-13 (csv == p.toString()).
findings.fix: Add verifyNoMoreInteractions(products). For the variant and offer lines, also assert line.variantId(), line.offerId() and line.sellerId() against the fixture.

findings.issue: findDetailsByIds repeats the findAllById, byId-map and LinkedHashSet-order loop of findByIds. The only differences are the active filter and the mapper.
findings.fix: Optionally extract a private orderedKnown(ids) helper that returns List<Product> in request order, and use it in both methods.

summary: PR-B matches the design. draft now makes one ProductBatchFeignClient.batch(csv, true) call over the distinct product ids. A requested id missing from the result (or a null body or 404) gives PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE before store.save, and the AC-14 test asserts zero orders and no reserveStock. Other Feign errors go to RemoteCalls.unavailable (503), behind the same per-host breaker. Prices, names and images come only from ProductView. Skipping variant stock is not a behaviour change on the money path. ProductViewFeignClient.Variant has no availableQuantity field, and neither OrderService nor PricingService reads stock from the view. The offer availableQuantity used by the buy-box filter in product-service OfferService:157 is still filled by offer enrichment. Caps hold. cartSnapshot rejects more than 50 cart lines and buyNowLines rejects more than 50 merged lines (MAX_LINES = 50), so distinct ids never exceed 50, and the endpoint checks the cap on the pre-dedupe list. No chunking is needed. ORDER_PRODUCT_BATCH_READ_TIMEOUT_MS (default 5000, connect timeout 1 s) is scoped to its own contextId, is documented in env-descriptions and environment-variables, and stays well inside the gateway orderCb budget (10 s route, 11 s time limiter). AC-12 token forwarding is tested by running the registered CorrelationAndAuthForwardingInterceptor bean on the real ProductBatchFeignClient contract: the inbound bearer is forwarded, and the header is absent with no request context. The guard tests do assert what they claim: exactly one batch call with 50 distinct ids for a 50-line cart, one id for two lines of the same product, and a CodedException rather than an NPE for an omitted id. Remaining findings are minor. The javadoc and test name wrongly say no inventory call is made. The parity test only covers products with no variant stock to report. AC-10 could also assert verifyNoMoreInteractions and the variant, offer and seller ids. The lean-default golden is byte-compared, and the lean code path is unchanged. Approved.
